title: Canary Deployment and Automatic Rollback
prompt: You want a production Lambda alias to initially route only 10% of traffic to a new version and automatically roll back to the previous version when a CloudWatch alarm goes off. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Configure a Lambda canary deployment and automatic rollback with CodeDeploy.
choices.explanation: This supports gradual deployment to a weighted alias and can be linked to alarms.

choices.text: Change only the reserved concurrency for the new version.
choices.explanation: This does not manage the traffic split or roll back to the previous version.

choices.text: Update all traffic to the new version and notify an operator afterward.
choices.explanation: This provides neither validation under partial traffic nor automatic rollback.

learning.reason: This supports gradual deployment to a weighted alias and can be linked to alarms.
learning.concept: For deployment alarms, choose metrics that indicate the health of the change, such as the user error rate.

title: Deploy to Many Accounts
prompt: You want common CloudFormation resources to be deployed automatically to accounts newly added to an OU. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Configure automatic deployment with Organizations-integrated, service-managed StackSets.
choices.explanation: This manages deployment to accounts added to the target OU.

choices.text: Create an organization trail in CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This aggregates operation records; it does not deploy templates.

choices.text: Manually create the same stack in each account.
choices.explanation: Future accounts will not receive the stack automatically.

learning.reason: This manages deployment to accounts added to the target OU.
learning.concept: Check the target OUs, Regions, concurrency, and failure tolerance before deployment.

title: Scheduled AMI Updates
prompt: You want to regularly patch and test a base AMI used by multiple teams before distributing it.

choices.text: Build a pipeline with EC2 Image Builder to create, test, and distribute the AMI.
choices.explanation: It can manage recurring updates to base images.

choices.text: Increase the desired capacity of an Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation: This changes the number of running instances but does not update the AMI contents.

choices.text: Manually patch only the running EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: New EC2 instances will still use the existing AMI unless it is updated separately.

learning.reason: It can manage recurring updates to base images.
learning.concept: Manage updates to existing instances separately from updates to the base image used when instances are recreated.

title: Automated Remediation Trigger
prompt: When a noncompliant S3 bucket is detected, you want to run an automated process to remediate it to an approved configuration.

choices.text: Combine an AWS Config rule with remediation using Systems Manager Automation.
choices.explanation: A compliance evaluation can trigger a predefined remediation.

choices.text: Review CloudTrail event history on a schedule.
choices.explanation: This lets you track actions but does not perform remediation.

choices.text: Set up only a billing alarm.
choices.explanation: A change in charges cannot determine whether a bucket configuration is noncompliant.

learning.reason: A compliance evaluation can trigger a predefined remediation.
learning.concept: Limit remediation permissions to the required resources and actions, and keep the process consistent when it runs again.

title: Reducing Notifications with a Composite Alarm
prompt: You want to notify the on-call team only when the error rate also worsens, rather than notifying them when CPU usage is high by itself.

choices.text: Use a CloudWatch composite alarm with an AND condition for both alarms to be in the ALARM state.
choices.explanation: It can combine the states of individual alarms to control notifications.

choices.text: Only increase the metrics retention period.
choices.explanation: This does not affect how notification conditions are combined.

choices.text: Connect both individual alarms directly to the same SNS topic.
choices.explanation: A threshold breach in either alarm would trigger a notification.

learning.reason: It can combine the states of individual alarms to control notifications.
learning.concept: If the individual alarms use different evaluation periods, also check when their ALARM states overlap.

title: Detecting Failed Deployments in ECS
prompt: For an ECS service using a rolling update, you want to return to the last healthy deployment if new tasks cannot start or pass health checks.

choices.text: Enable rollback for the ECS deployment circuit breaker.
choices.explanation: It can detect a failed deployment and return to the previous healthy deployment.
This controls how long build artifacts are retained; it does not recover from a task startup failure.

choices.text: Only increase the number of containers and continue.
choices.explanation: The startup failure remains, and no rollback to the previous deployment is configured.

learning.reason: It can detect a failed deployment and return to the previous healthy deployment.
learning.concept: Design for detecting startup failures as well as cases where application metrics worsen after startup.
